neighbours.label: ' in the' / ' on the' in a stock locative phrase, anticipating the household medium noun (in the mirror, on the radio, in the newspaper, in the refrigerator, in the mail); quiet on 'in/on the' before an ordinary place
fire: Before the interview he glanced at himself in the mirror one last time.
My grandmother still listens to the football results on the radio every Saturday.
You should take a long hard look at yourself in the mirror, my friend.
Cover the dough and let it rest in the refrigerator for an hour.
Her father read about the accident in the newspaper the following day.
The children made silly faces at themselves in the mirror all afternoon.
Your new membership card should arrive in the mail within ten days.
They first heard that song on the radio during a long drive.
quiet: Before the interview he glanced at the clock one last time.
My grandmother still walks to the football ground on the hill every Saturday.
You should take a long hard look at the contract, my friend.
Cover the dough and let it rest under a cloth for an hour.
Her father talked about the accident with the neighbours the following day.
The children made silly faces at each other in the garden all afternoon.
Your new membership card should be ready at the front desk within ten days.
They first sang that song in the car during a long drive.

notes: Card: peaks on ' the'/' in' before mirror, refrigerator, radio, mail; output promotes ' news', ' newspaper', ' mail'. Probes: mirror 0.70, newspaper 0.46, radio 0.31, fridge 0.30, mail 0.20; park 0.05, fence 0.00.
